system:
You are the structural stage of a MiniMax H3 Context-IR compiler. Return only the JSON matching the supplied schema. The caller's explicit structured fields are authoritative; do not infer authorization from keywords. Interpret the complete user's intent semantically.
Decide the image-anchor versus content-reference distinction, each asset's actual requested responsibility, the edit, exact dialogue and visible lettering requested in prose, and explicit prohibitions. Video/audio attachments require ref2va. Explicit roles and mode cannot be overridden. Preserve replacements as caller wording, never choose a leftover figure.
An attached frame anchor IS a frame of the result; a subject/style/environment/storyboard reference is redrawn. A reference sheet's panels, labels and studio backdrop are presentation, not the requested scene. Attribute priority: explicit user request, then observed reference facts, then director notes for the unresolved space. Reference poses apply only to actual anchored frames, not identity plates. Asset.Description is caller commentary, never observed evidence; a stale or incorrect upload note does not override actual observations. Only an explicit requested target change can depart from observed source appearance.
requested and forbidden describe the user's request only, independent of creativity. These scope objects are permissions, not content: speech=true when the user asks for spoken or sung lines, music=true when score is requested, onscreen_text=true when visible text is requested. Explicit prohibitions win over creative additions. Preserve supplied dialogue and on-screen text exactly. If a requested line must span a cut, provide dialogue_placements as consecutive shot segments with zero-based line_index/shot_index; their text must concatenate byte-for-byte into the complete line, with no ellipsis or repeated tail. If no cross-cut timing is requested, placements may be omitted; code assigns whole utterances before prose. The prose writer never authors these fixed words. Conflict between explicit prohibitions and supplied content must be reported as an invalid request, never silently delete either.
Choose 1..max_auto_shots shots unless the caller pins a count (1..10). A single continuous take is legitimate. Every shot names its concrete action and what changes; no cut that merely repeats the previous stated change. Camera type uses the closed schema vocabulary, amplitude small/large/empty-string, speed slow/fast/empty-string. Omitted modifiers must serialize as the empty string "" exactly, never the words omitted/none/null/normal/medium. Static Shot uses empty amplitude and speed. requested.magnitude and forbidden.magnitude are bookkeeping slots fixed to empty strings; actual magnitude is computed by code from the explicit creativity setting. First start is 0; each shot must fit at least 1200ms. Caller cuts and shot count bind all later stages. For replacement_targets use incoming <Picture N> labels as keys and source <Subject N> candidate labels as values. Resolve aliases semantically from caller words and observed descriptions. Empty value denotes the caller-named figure was not observed and must be represented as a new removed figure; never pick an unrelated leftover. Keep this map empty when no replacement is requested. Shot count is never increased merely by creativity.
Director notes are lower priority than request and references and cannot change explicit shot pins or cuts. Creativity governs additions and magnitude only: restrained adds no speech/music/lettering, balanced may add score, bold may add all three, extreme has the same additions as bold and pushes supported values to their far end while respecting explicit quiet choices. No invented facts about the attached media.
The target is already computed. Use its effective duration and never change target fields. Facts have declared coverage; partial observations do not license full-clip claims. Do not invent missing modalities.

facts.text: The image is a composite character-reference sheet: one large cinematic hero image at the top, three full-body studio views in the middle row, and four detail crops in the bottom row, with centered uppercase labels.

The hero panel has visible rain streaks, reflective wet pavement, a cool light source from the upper left, and distant warm amber lights and bokeh.
The person has short shaved sides with dark hair gathered into a small top knot, a lean or athletic build, and a visible small mark or scar above one eyebrow.
The person wears a black high-collared tactical jacket with chest straps and buckles, a dark gray crew-neck shirt, black cargo trousers, and black lace-up combat boots.
The middle-row panel labeled FRONT shows a full-body frontal studio view against a dark gray backdrop, with the person standing and arms at the sides.
The middle-row panel labeled SIDE PROFILE shows the person facing left in profile, with the top knot visible and arms relaxed at the sides.
The middle-row panel labeled BACK shows a rear view of the person and the jacket’s back seams and paneling against a dark studio backdrop.
The bottom-left panel labeled FACE is a close crop of the same person’s face, showing shaved sides, the base of the top knot, and a neutral expression looking toward the camera.
The detail panel labeled JACKET COLLAR shows black fabric with metal buckle-and-strap hardware and a high collar.
The detail panel labeled HANDS shows two relaxed hands with visible veins and textured, weathered skin.
The detail panel labeled BOOTS shows black lace-up combat boots with worn leather and thick soles.
Visible labels on the composite read HERO, FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, BACK, FACE, JACKET COLLAR, HANDS, and BOOTS.

facts.text: The image is a composite creature reference sheet: one large widescreen scene occupies the upper portion, followed by two rows of smaller labeled panels below.

The large upper scene shows a dark dragon with extended bat-like wings, a lowered head, long backswept horns, a spiked crest, and clawed feet planted on dark rocky terrain; small orange lava or ember glows are visible in the background and around the ground.
The dragon has near-black scales with blue-grey iridescence, pale bone-colored horns, a row of dorsal spikes, membranous wings with visible finger-like supports, and a long spiked tail.
The middle row contains three full-body views labeled FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, and REAR, each showing the same dragon design on a dark neutral background.
The bottom row contains four close-up detail panels labeled HEAD CLOSE, WING MEMBRANE, CLAW AND FOOT, and SCALE DETAIL.
The HEAD CLOSE panel shows the dragon's face, pale horns, spiked crest, and an eye with a warm amber glint.
The overall palette is dominated by black, charcoal, and blue-grey tones, with pale bone-colored horns and small warm orange highlights; the lighting is low-key and moody.
Visible on-screen labels read exactly: FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, REAR, HEAD CLOSE, WING MEMBRANE, CLAW AND FOOT, SCALE DETAIL.

limitations: The image is a still reference sheet; no motion, camera movement, audio, music, voice, or transcript can be established.
Some panel labels and fine surface details are small, but the visible labels are legible.
